finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id deletes any project without an ownership check because authorized() return value is discarded at api.js:18.
finding.source: Route parameter req.params.id (api.js:16), attacker is any authenticated user.

trace.note: project loaded by attacker-supplied id with no ownership scoping
authorized(req.user, project) called; boolean result ignored

finding.guards_checked: authorized() (api.js:12-14) returns boolean and does not throw; its result is unused. Sibling PUT handler (api.js:25) uses throwing authorize() and is enforced. Upstream auth middleware not present in repo, unverified.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at api.js:18, so its result is discarded; no ownership check runs before projects.delete at api.js:19. The only other file in the directory is api.js itself, so there is no other middleware in the repo to enforce ownership. The sibling PUT handler at api.js:25 uses the throwing authorize() at api.js:4-10, which is not applied to DELETE.
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:18 calls authorized() as a bare statement and discards its boolean, so api.js:19 deletes the project for any caller who passes upstream authentication, which is the authenticated low-privilege user the finding describes.
